presets.label: Lowest latency
presets.description: Keeps the AMD encoder on its fastest settings and limits every frame, recovery keyframes included, to one frame's share of the bitrate, so a lost frame costs less time on the wire.

evidence.amd_max_frame_size: rust/PERFORMANCE.md, "October 7, 2026: AMF rate control and recovery keyframes", "Decision and limits": a one-frame cap cut the largest recovery frame of 4K40 HEVC by 66% (265,995 to 89,626 bytes) with the same steady-state frame sizes and encode time within 0.1 ms.
evidence.amd_quality: rust/PERFORMANCE.md, "October 7: AMF split-frame encoding", quality preset rows: the quality preset costs 1.0 ms (HEVC) and 12 ms (AV1) per 4K60 frame over speed.
evidence.amd_preanalysis: rust/PERFORMANCE.md, same table: pre-analysis takes 25 ms per 4K60 frame (HEVC and AV1) against 5-6 ms without.

presets.label: Reference quality
presets.description: Spends the whole bitrate on the picture: constant bitrate, and no size limit on recovery keyframes. Frames get larger, so it suits a fast, steady link.

evidence.amd_rc: rust/PERFORMANCE_WORK.md, "AMF settings per codec: quality at a given bitrate": constant bitrate raised VMAF by up to 0.5 (HEVC), 0.3 (AV1) and 1.0 (H.264) on the first clip and moved it by -0.75 to +0.24 on the second, with the same encode time. The 99th-percentile frame grows by 30-67%. Small and content-dependent; HDR rows were -0.23 to +0.48.
evidence.amd_max_frame_size: rust/PERFORMANCE.md, "Decision and limits": the cap lowered encoded payload from 64 to 51 Mbps in the 63 Mbps recovery run, so removing it keeps recovery keyframes at full quality.
